pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
It is my great pleasure to welcome you to The Blue School website. The Blue is a remarkable school. Our school is built around our collective community of wonderful individuals, working toward a shared vision. That makes our school a vibrant and exciting place to study and work.
The Blue has served the City of Wells and its surrounding communities since 1641. That history is important to us. It creates an exceptionally strong common ethos that binds generations of families, all of whom have passed through the school. Our core values – respect, empathy, politeness – have been fundamental to the school for over three centuries and continue to serve our community well.
Building on our status as a Research School, we have established ourselves as a centre of excellence for teaching. Our broad, creative curriculum strives to give our students a social and academic belonging. Combining close, personal pastoral care, with high academic standards, our students develop the wide range of skills necessary to thrive in the modern world and lead a physically, mentally and spiritually healthy life.
We are proud to be a Church school and believe that this supports the emphasis on our core values for all our students. Developing a community belonging for students of a Christian or non-Christian faith, and for those of no faith, remains very important to us.
I hope that our website gives you a flavour of life at The Blue. Please do contact us if you wish to find out more about studying or working at our school.
Mark Woodlock, Headteacher

pageCache.text:
Welcome to our Virtual 6th Form Open Event
Welcome from the Headteacher
Mr Woodlock
We hope that this Virtual 6th Form Open Evening will be useful if you are unable to attend our event in school. It is also intended as a means for those who need to check on information about our courses and hope it will give you a flavour of life in the 6th form so that you can make an informed choice about this - very important - next stage in your education.
Our prospectus contains the information you need about the courses we offer. Once you have had a look at the subjects in which you are interested, please complete an application form and hand it in at Reception. Alternatively, you can send it to SixthForm@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk or post it to the school. No decisions are absolute at this stage – you can change your mind about what you want to study. We just need your initial thoughts so we can discuss them with you during your 6th form interview. If you need to talk things through with staff before you complete your form, please seek out the relevant teachers who will be more than happy to talk to you.
For those of you new to the school, please do not hesitate to contact us if you require further information about our courses of study. We will be very happy to hear from you and to put you in touch with our helpful staff. Please call Jo Stitch on 01749 836251 or email jstitch@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk.

Parents/Carers' Evening Booking System
Our online Booking System can be used to make your Parent/Carer appointments via the link below.
The booking facility will become available online a few days prior to the event taking place and details will be sent to you.
https://theblue.schoolcloud.co.uk/Please note - if the system is not open for bookings a 'Sorry but this website address does not exist' message may appear.
Some of our parent/carer evenings will take place remotely and you will be informed as to whether the meeting you are invited to will be in person or virtual. Where an evening will take place virtually, please click on the link below to view our instructions on how to participate in these events.

pageCache.text:
News
A Level and BTEC Results 2026
Blue School A Level results
Students at The Blue School are celebrating a marvellous set of A Level and BTEC outcomes as a consequence of this year’s results.
Despite the unique and challenging circumstances that they have faced in their secondary education, coping with a pandemic and crumbling concrete, this cohort of students have seen a true reward for their effort, application and tenacity. 60% of all entries were graded A*-B and nearly 90% all entries were at grade C or above.
The vast majority of our students have been offered their first-choice university place or are able to embark upon their chosen career path. These include a number of places at the most competitive universities and courses across the country and a wide range of careers, from law to architecture, sport to engineering, politics to biochemistry.
Headteacher, Mark Woodlock, commented, ‘I am incredibly proud of the achievements of all of our students this year. That is true for both the individuals themselves and for the teachers and school staff that have supported them to get to this point. We hope that these results will give them the best platform for the next steps in their education and careers.
‘They have proved themselves an exemplar group of role models. For that reason, we know that they will contribute to a positive future.
‘These results are the product of the close partnership between ourselves and the local community. We thank all of those who have supported these students during their time at school, particularly in the last few years. We believe that our community should be justifiably proud of its students and of the school that serves Wells and the surrounding area.’

Special Educational Needs and Disabilities
The Blue School's Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-ordinator (SENDCo) is Mrs Anna Honeyands.
If you are a parent/carer and have concerns about your child's learning and enjoyment of school around known or potential SEND, please do not hesitate to contact Mrs Honeyands. Mrs Honeyands can be contacted via the school tel: 01749 678799 email: SENOffice@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk.
If you are a student and want to talk to someone about help with your learning or support in school, please talk to your Tutor in the first instance. They will arrange for you to speak to the right person in school who can help you. This may be Mrs Honeyands or another member of staff in the school.
Mrs Honeyands is supported by Mrs Sally Chinn, SEND Team Administrator and Miss Katie Biddiscombe, SEND (EHCP) Administrator.
A team of Teaching Assistants work closely with students and staff across the school site, offering a range of tailored provision in class, in small groups or 1:1, depending on individual needs.

Careers
Beyond the Blue
Your career is the pathway you choose to follow through learning and work.
As a student at the Blue, Careers is here to support you through the process of deciding what direction you would like to take when you leave school, and ensure that you develop the skills needed for a successful working and fulfilling life.
Our programme of Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance is progressive. From Year 7 onwards, you will be encouraged to reflect on careers choices, have meaningful encounters with employers and experiences of the workplace and research your career path in structured learning time.
In Year 11 and Sixth Form, you will get more support to be able to make decisions about Post-16 and 18 routes, including through meetings with independent careers advisors and workshops on different aspects of life and careers. We support you by hosting events which offer a full picture of opportunities in Higher Education, employment, Apprenticeships and other professional and technical qualifications.
Careers Contacts
Students in years 7 to 11 - Ms Watson
Based in the Kennion Vestibule. Email careers@theblueschoolwells.co.uk or by phoning 01749-678799 and asking for Careers.
Ms Wendy Watson is our Careers and Work Experience Co-ordinator and also a qualified Careers Adviser. She offers 1-1 Careers meetings with all students in Year 11 and Year 12 and with other students on request.
Her working days are Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and alternate Fridays.
Post-16 students - Mrs Hole
Based in the Sixth Form Centre. Email at sixthform@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk or by phoning 01749-678799 x413.
You can also call the National Careers Helpline to talk to an adviser about your career options: 0800 100 900
Mr Bilkey, Assistant Headteacher is the Leadership team member responsible for Careers and can be contacted at abilkey@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk.
The Link Governor for Careers is Mr Darrell Frost who can be contacted via Mrs Stitch, Clerk to Governors email govsclerk@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk.
We have business Enterprise Advisers (EAs), Mike Bristowe from Airbus and Martin Symons from Heidelberg Materials, who are linked to our school and offer support from a business perspective on our careers curriculum.
Support for Parents/Carers helping your child with careers choices
If you are a parent/carer and wish to hav some advice to help your child with their careers choices or to arrange a one-to-one careers appointment for your child, please contact Ms Watson by email: careers@theblueschoolwells.co.uk.
Careers Programme
Click here for the 2026/27 Careers Programme - Learning Journey and Objectives.
Our programme links to the Gatsby Benchmarks which have been accepted as best practice by the Government. They are:
1. A stable careers programme 2. Learning from careers and labour market information 3. Addressing the needs of each student 4. Linking curriculum learning to careers 5. Encounters with employers and employees 6. Experiences of workplaces 7. Encounters with further and higher education 8. Personal guidance
We assess the school's careers provision against the Gatsby Benchmarks using the Compass+ tool, which enables us to track our students' career interests and intended destinations, actual destinations, careers activities and to keep a record of organisations that can support the school's careers provision.
We use Unifrog to provide students with expert information and resource tools. Each student can login using their school Google Mail account and can use the programme to record qualifications, experiences and skills to map out their plan for the future.
Parents can also create a login linked to their child's account and help them explore interests and ideas and research future options. Please click on the link below for further details:
Unifrog for parents/carers
We are also a member of the following networks and organisations designed to secure employer engagement with activities designed to encourage young people to find out and know more about local and national opportunities.
Somerset Careers Hub
Somerset Chamber of Commerce
Somerset Education Business Partnership
Careers in the Curriculum
As well as facilitating careers activities in the school, teachers add careers information into their lessons to help students understand the variety of jobs on offer. Lesson content may also touch on employability skills, such as presentation, teamwork and leadership.
This co-ordinated approach ensures that key skills and knowledge about career options, progression and success are embedded in our curriculum from Years 7 to 13. This allows our students to make links in their learning as well as develop the ability to think deeply about what they are learning and how this may impact on their future, whatever they decide to do.

Sports and Fitness for the Community
Wells Blue Sports Centre provides access to The Blue School's facilities for community use outside the school's operational hours.
Facilities available for community use include
Sport and Fitness Clubs and "private groups engaged in sport or fitness" are welcome to use our facilities for group bookings.
Members of the public can use our Fitness Suite including Weights Room on a adhoc basis (following Lite Induction) at £6.00 per session (paid on booking). Alternatively, a £20.00 non-contract monthly membership is available for access to facilities when WBSC is open.
Please contact Andy Jones, WBSC Manager at ajones@theblueschool.somerset.sch.uk or tel: 01749 836222.
Wells Blue Sports Centre
Also like our facebook page for regular updates.
Access via the Kennion Road Entrance to the school. Free car-parking available for WBSC users attending site.
WBSC Ltd is a subsidiary company of The Blue School, which is the sole shareholder. WBSC Ltd operates the community aspects of the school's operations, outside the objectives of The Blue School, a state maintained school under the Academies Act 2010.
